=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- File: .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml
  Line or code reference: Lines 52, 82 — `!contains(fromJson('["false"]'), vars.CHECK_FAILURE_TRIAGE_ENABLED)`
  Problem: GitHub Actions `contains()` is case-sensitive. This expression only matches the exact lowercase string "false". If a consumer sets `CHECK_FAILURE_TRIAGE_ENABLED` to `FALSE` or `False` (natural variants users might type), the YAML gate passes and the workflow incurs checkout/codex-install costs before the shell script's case-insensitive guard (`"${ENABLED,,}"`) exits. The shell script handles case-insensitivity; the YAML gates do not.
  Why it fails at runtime: Runner minutes and API quota are consumed for a no-op triage when the variable is set to a non-lowercase false value. The triage does execute (correct behavior from a triage standpoint) but wastes ~30-60 seconds of runner time and one `gh api` paginated call per occurrence. This is a pre-existing defect from the earlier `!= 'false'` gate that persists through this autofix run — the `contains` array approach was meant to harden case-sensitivity but GitHub Actions `contains` on strings is case-sensitive, unlike Bash's `==`.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
